Web design San Jose businesses need in the Bay Area's largest city

San Jose is the most populous city in the Bay Area and in Northern California, with close to a million residents. A city that size does not have one shopping district. It has dozens of small ones, and customers think in those names, not in "San Jose." Here are a few, with what a website for a business there should keep in mind.

Japantown

One of only three surviving historic Japantowns in the United States, alongside San Francisco's and Los Angeles's, and the youngest of the three. In December 2025 the California Arts Council named it a California Cultural District, for 2026 through 2030. A shop here has history on its side and should say so.

Willow Glen

Southwest of downtown, with Lincoln Avenue as its main street and, by the city visitor bureau's count, more than 250 businesses along it. A site for a business here should name the street and the cross street.

SoFA

The South First Area, centered on three blocks of South First Street between Reed and San Carlos. Independent businesses adopted the name in the early 1990s, and the monthly South First Fridays art walk still draws evening crowds. Galleries and bars here need event dates that are actually current.

Story Road

The stretch of Story Road near McLaughlin Avenue is widely known as Little Saigon, the center of the city's large Vietnamese American community. What to call the district officially was a long city council fight in 2007 and 2008, but customers use the Little Saigon name when they search.

Alum Rock and Berryessa

East and north San Jose neighborhoods, with Little Portugal inside Alum Rock and the Berryessa Flea Market to the north. Service businesses here often draw from the whole East Side, so a page per area they cover makes sense.

Santana Row

A mixed-use shopping and residential district on the west side, between Stevens Creek and Winchester Boulevards. A small shop near a district this busy needs a page that makes clear where it is and how to reach it.

One owner, one search, start to finish

An illustration, not a client: a bakery owner on Lincoln Avenue who has only ever had a social media page.

A family new to Willow Glen searches "birthday cake near me" on a Saturday morning. Google shows a map with three pins. Two of the bakeries have websites with their hours, a cake order form and photos of real cakes. The third, ours in this story, shows only a social page with posts from last month and no hours. The family taps one of the other two.

Now give that bakery a five-page site. The home page says what it bakes and that it is on Lincoln Avenue. A cakes page lists sizes, flavors and how many days' notice it needs. The contact page has the hours, a map and a form that emails every order request to the owner. Nothing fancy. It simply answers the questions the family had before they had to ask, and that is often the difference between a call and a scroll past.

That is the Starter package at $497, live in 7 to 14 days, and the owner owns it outright.

Website design in San Jose that wins the map

Google says local results turn mostly on relevance, distance and prominence: how well a listing matches the search, how close it is, and how well known the business is. In a city spread across this much ground, distance settles a lot by itself; a dentist in Evergreen is rarely shown to someone searching in North San Jose.

Relevance is where a website pulls its weight. A page that names your neighborhood, lists your actual services and matches your Google Business Profile gives Google something specific to work with. Pro includes Google Business Profile setup and schema markup for exactly that reason. It cannot promise a top spot, and neither will we.

Designer, company or agency: what each one means in San Jose

People search for a San Jose web design company, a web design agency, a website designer or web development, often for the same small job. The words point at different kinds of help.

  • Web design agencyA team: strategy, design, copy, development and account management. Right for a brand with a large budget and many moving parts.
  • Web design companyOften a smaller shop with a few designers and developers. Prices vary widely; ask what is included and what is billed monthly.
  • Website designerOne person, usually responsible for the look and the pages. Ask who writes the words and who owns the finished site.
  • Web developmentThe engineering side: databases, custom features, integrations. Most neighborhood businesses need very little of it beyond a working contact form.

We sit in the third row. One person writes and builds each site, and you deal with him directly.

Where San Jose owners get advice for free

BusinessOwnerSpace

The City of San Jose's small business network, which connects entrepreneurs to information, technical help and partner organizations such as SCORE.

Silicon Valley SBDC

Hosted by San Jose State University and funded with support from the SBA and the state's GO-Biz office, it offers free or low-cost advising and training to Santa Clara County businesses from its office on Monterey Road.

SCORE Silicon Valley

Free volunteer mentoring and workshops. The chapter works through the San Jose Chamber of Commerce and mentors by appointment over phone, video or email.

San Jose Chamber of Commerce

The city's chamber, which went by The Silicon Valley Organization for several years before returning to the San Jose Chamber of Commerce name.

Common questions

How much do web designers charge for a website in San Jose?

There is no single local rate. Freelancers, small studios and Silicon Valley agencies all price differently, and many give a number only after a call. Our prices are printed: Starter is $497 for five pages, Pro is $997 for ten pages plus ten city pages, and Agency is $1,997 for research-led pages across your whole area, each paid once. Hosting, maintenance and updates add $49 a month. If you keep an AI agent (the Pro chat widget after its 14-day free trial, or the Agency phone agent after its 7-day trial), it is $297 a month and hosting is included in that.

Should I hire a San Jose web design company or a single website designer?

A company gives you a team and charges for it. A single designer gives you one person who does the work and answers the questions. We are the second kind: Maurice Johnson writes and builds every site himself. The trade-off is that he works from East Texas, so there are no in-person meetings in San Jose.

Do you also do web development in San Jose?

For a small business site, yes: the pages are designed, written and built, the contact form emails you every lead, and titles, descriptions, sitemap and schema are set up for search. Custom software such as a booking system tied to your own database or a large online store is a different kind of project, and our packages do not include it. We will say so before you buy.

Can a website designer outside San Jose, CA write about my neighborhood accurately?

Only if he asks you and checks the facts, which is how we work. You tell us the streets you are on, the parts of town your customers come from and what makes your shop different. Maurice researches the rest from public sources and you review every page before it goes live.

What should a San Jose shop put on its home page first?

What you sell, the neighborhood you are in, your hours and a phone number that dials on one tap. Then one sentence on why a customer should choose you over the shop a mile away. Everything else can live one click deeper.

See your website before you pay for it

Give us your business name and what you do, and a demo site gets built for you to look at on your own phone. If you like it, pick a package. If you do not, you have spent nothing but the minute it took to look.
